## Summary

Remove the Java authoring DSL (`pathland-view`) entirely and make **Kotlin the only JVM authoring DSL** before 1.0.

The JVM engine/runtime (`pathland-view-core`) stays; the Kotlin DSL (`pathland-view-kotlin`) becomes the sole supported way to author JVM views. Java is no longer an authoring target, though it remains an implementation/host language where needed.

## Motivation

- One JVM authoring surface instead of two.
- Stop maintaining duplicate Java/Kotlin view and modifier surfaces.
- Avoid Java/Kotlin API drift and repeated parity work.
- Align the JVM story with the Kotlin-first direction.
- Remove Java-only build machinery (`State` annotation processor, Java constructor-enforcement processor).
- Make future work (including a possible KMP spike) easier by having one JVM DSL.

## Current state

- Java DSL: `lib/java/pathland-view` — 101 files, ~8.1k LOC, ~4.6k lines of tests.
- Java-only processor: `lib/java/pathland-view-processor` (`State` binding + authoring-convention checks).
- Kotlin DSL: `lib/java/pathland-view-kotlin` — Kotlin-owned views/modifiers over `pathland-view-core`, currently JVM-only.
- Java DSL is used by:
  - `pathland-demo-views` (36 files, ~2.7k LOC)
  - `pathland-gtk-demo`
  - `pathland-qt-demo`
  - `pathland-quarkus-demo`
  - `pathland-spring-boot-demo`
  - Java tests in `pathland-server-core`, `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-quarkus`, and `pathland-spring-boot-starter`
  - `pathland-spring-boot-starter` production dependency
  - `pathland-quarkus-java` + `pathland-quarkus-starter`
- Kotlin parity tests currently use the Java DSL as a test-scope oracle.
- `spec/DSL.md`, `README.md`, and `AGENTS.md` are still Java-centric.

## Decisions

input.command: gh issue view 169 2>&1 | sed -n '50,200p'; echo "---BRANCHES---"; git branch -a | tail -30

result.output:
- Java authoring is a non-goal.
- Kotlin is the only JVM authoring DSL.
- Removal happens before 1.0; breaking changes are acceptable.
- Java GTK and Qt demos will be ported to Kotlin, not dropped.
- The Java core API is not necessarily public. Keep `pathland-view-core` as needed for the engine/SPI, but document it as an implementation/SPI surface, not an authoring API.
- Keep the artifact name `pathland-view-kotlin`; do not reuse the old `pathland-view` name for Kotlin.
- Kotlin Multiplatform support is explicitly out of scope for this issue.

## Scope

### Remove

- [ ] `lib/java/pathland-view`
- [ ] `lib/java/pathland-view-processor`
- [ ] `pathland-quarkus-java`
- [ ] `pathland-quarkus-java-deployment`
- [ ] `pathland-quarkus-starter` compatibility alias
- [ ] Java Quarkus demo (`pathland-quarkus-demo`) once the Kotlin demo covers it
- [ ] Java DSL test-scope dependencies everywhere
- [ ] Java DSL release artifacts and documentation references

### Keep

- [ ] `pathland-view-core` as the JVM engine/SPI
- [ ] `pathland-view-kotlin` as the sole JVM authoring DSL
- [ ] `pathland-quarkus` (DSL-neutral) and `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`
- [ ] `pathland-server-core`, renderers, state, test kit

### Port to Kotlin

- [ ] `pathland-demo-views` (use `KotlinView` + `state()`)
- [ ] `pathland-gtk-demo` host code
- [ ] `pathland-qt-demo` host code
- [ ] `pathland-spring-boot-demo`
- [ ] Java test fixtures in `pathland-server-core`, `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-quarkus`, and `pathland-spring-boot-starter`
- [ ] Rename/update Java-specific demo run scripts

## Migration plan

### Phase 0 — Land the current in-flight refactors

- JVM engine split + Kotlin ownership.
- Quarkus core/Java/Kotlin extension split + Kotlin demo.
- These are transitional; the Java Quarkus extension and starter alias are deleted in Phase 3.

### Phase 1 — Make Kotlin independently conformant

- [ ] Move engine/runtime tests from `pathland-view` into `pathland-view-core`.
- [ ] Move DSL-level tests into `pathland-view-kotlin` and rewrite them in Kotlin.
- [ ] Replace Java-vs-Kotlin parity tests with Kotlin-only golden frame assertions.
- [ ] Run the shared engine traces through Kotlin.
- [ ] Cover every primitive, modifier, control, navigation path, media path, and `ViewThatFits`.
- [ ] Remove `pathland-view-kotlin`'s test-scope dependency on `pathland-view`.

Acceptance: Kotlin tests no longer need the Java DSL for confidence.

### Phase 2 — Port JVM demos to Kotlin

- [ ] Rewrite `pathland-demo-views` in Kotlin.
- [ ] Port GTK host to Kotlin; update run script.
- [ ] Port Qt host to Kotlin; update run script.
- [ ] Port Spring Boot demo to Kotlin.
- [ ] Delete the Java Quarkus demo; keep `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo`.
- [ ] Optionally have the Kotlin Quarkus demo mount the ported shared `MusicPlayerView`.

Acceptance: every surviving demo builds and runs without `pathland-view`.

### Phase 3 — Remove Java DSL and Java integrations

- [ ] Remove `pathland-view` and `pathland-view-processor` modules.
- [ ] Remove `pathland-quarkus-java`, its deployment module, and the starter alias.
- [ ] Make `pathland-spring-boot-starter` DSL-neutral.
- [ ] Remove Java DSL test dependencies from all modules.
- [ ] Add an Enforcer ban for `dev.pathland:pathland-view`.
- [ ] Remove Java DSL artifacts from the release workflow.

### Phase 4 — Docs/spec/status

- [ ] Rewrite `spec/DSL.md` around Kotlin; remove Java realization tables/sections.
- [ ] Update `README.md` examples and demo table.
- [ ] Update `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `RELEASING.md`.
- [ ] Update/delete affected `status.md` files.
- [ ] Add a migration note for Java users.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mvn -q -B test` passes.
- [ ] No production or test dependency on `dev.pathland:pathland-view`.
- [ ] `pathland-view`, `pathland-view-processor`, `pathland-quarkus-java`, and `pathland-quarkus-starter` no longer exist.
- [ ] Kotlin Quarkus demo, Spring Boot demo, GTK demo, and Qt demo all run on Kotlin-authored views.
- [ ] Release workflow publishes only the surviving JVM libraries.
- [ ] Docs/spec no longer present Java as the JVM reference realization.
- [ ] Existing Rust `pathland-view` crate is untouched.

## Risks / notes

- Kotlin's current test suite is much smaller than the Java DSL's; Phase 1 is mandatory before deletion.
- Spring Boot's Kotlin/compiler version must be aligned and tested.
- Root Kotlin is currently 2.2.20 while the Quarkus Kotlin extension/demo use 2.4.10; settle one version matrix before the port.
- Do not cut a release between the transitional Quarkus work and the removal if the transitional Java extension should not be published.
- Need to decide whether the Spring Boot starter remains core-only or gets a Kotlin convenience starter.

## Open questions

- Keep `pathland-view-kotlin` as the permanent artifact name? (Recommended: yes.)
- Should the Spring Boot starter stay core-only, with apps adding `pathland-view-kotlin`, or should there be a `pathland-spring-boot-kotlin` convenience artifact?
- Is `pathland-view-core` documented as public SPI or internal implementation detail?
- Which Kotlin version becomes the project-wide baseline?

- `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-java/`, `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-starter/`
- `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/`

# pathland-demo-views-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

Kotlin-owned demo views over `pathland-view-kotlin`, with no Java-DSL dependency.
The first (and currently only) view is the app-driven music player.

## Implemented

- **`MusicPlayerView`** — Apple Music-style root: one root `SizeThatFits`
  selects narrow (no volume), medium (volume), or wide (volume + `NowPlayingSidebar`),
  with the floating `PlayerBar`.
- **Persisted player state** — `player.position`, `player.playing`,
  `player.track`, `player.volume`, `player.seekRequest`, `player.volumeRequest`
  via Kotlin `KotlinView` state delegates.
- **App-driven media** — a `MediaController` owns the source/transport; every
  fit candidate shares the same controller. `MEDIA_*` reports feed position/volume
  and `MEDIA_ENDED` advances the track.
- **Seek/volume decoupling** — `SeekControl` buffers drags and commits on release;
  `PercentSeek` maps seconds to 0..100; `VolumeControl` separates report from
  command.
- **Lyrics** — synchronized two-line karaoke pill driven by the parsed SRT cues.
- **Window metadata** — track-derived title/description and `locale("en")`.
- **Sponsored proxy** — optional `adUrl` appends a `ProxyView` in the sidebar.
- **Accessibility** — transport labels, slider labels, `MAIN`/`HEADER` roles.

- Remaining demo views (KitchenSink, SplitNav, AdView) are still Java; tracked by
  #169.

`mvn test -pl pathland-demo-views-kotlin` — `LyricsTest`, `SeekControlTest`,
`MusicPlayerViewTest` (tree/render, fit swaps, media state, seek echo guard,

# pathland-view-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

The idiomatic Kotlin authoring surface (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`). Phase 3 is
complete: every production view/modifier is Kotlin-owned over
`pathland-view-core`; the Java DSL is a test-scope parity oracle only.

## Phase 3

- **Core-owned in Kotlin**: all primitives, shapes, stacks, grids, scroll/lazy
  containers, `ForEach`, `Button`, text/value controls, media, navigation,
  `Label`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`, `ProxyView`, and the complete modifier
  vocabulary (padding/frame/fonts/colors/borders/shadows/effects/transforms/
  interaction/accessibility/environment/styles/window metadata).
- **Dependency boundary**: main depends on `pathland-view-core` only; the Java
  DSL is test-scope for byte-for-byte parity comparisons.
- Tests compare the Kotlin-owned views and modifiers against the Java DSL.

## Implemented

- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`, `Rectangle`,
  `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`,
  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
- **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
  `ProxyView`.
- **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
  `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
  `ColorPicker`.
- **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
  `.children(...)`. A custom `KotlinView` constructed inline in a block
  auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`
  inside `body()` (it does not leak into the enclosing scope). An explicit
  `view.add()` / `+view` is available for Java-constructed views (e.g.
  `mediaController.attach()`).
- **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
  `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`, `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
- **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
  layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
  foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
  visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
  environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents. A child
  modifier replaces its auto-registered leaf in the enclosing builder, so
  `VStack { Text("x").fontSize(20f) }` keeps the modifier. The Java
  `.modifiers(...)` operation remains available as an escape hatch.
- **Persisted state**: `KotlinView` base class + `val count by state(0)`
  (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
  form for two-way controls. Bound to the session's `PersistentState` before the
  first `body()` render — no kapt and no annotation processor.
- **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
  list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
- **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
  `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
- **Media**: `Video(controller)`; audio remains view-less (`controller.attach()`
  can be added with `+`).
- **Tests**: byte-identical Kotlin-vs-Java frame comparison, auto-collection,
  child-modifier application, modifier property parity, fine-grained signal
  deltas, persisted/stateful bodies, reactive `ForEach`, two-way `TextField`,
  navigation swaps and link intents.

## Not implemented / gaps

- The Kotlin modifier config types (`Padding`, `Frame`, `Border`, `Shadow`,
  `ClipShape`, `Font`) are Kotlin ownership types; code migrating from the Java
  DSL should use the Kotlin `Modifiers` sugar instead of Java config classes.
- A Kotlin-native annotation processor is intentionally not used. `state(...)`
  works on `KotlinView` subclasses; a plain `View` implementation should use
  signals directly or extend `KotlinView`.
- No Kotlin Multiplatform target yet — the module is JVM-only over
  `pathland-view-core`.
- `SecureField` is Kotlin-owned (`TEXT_FIELD` + `IS_SECURE`).

import dev.pathland.view.core.FontWeight

import dev.pathland.view.dsl.ForEach

import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Text

import dev.pathland.view.dsl.fontWeight
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.frame
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.padding

/**
 * A small Kotlin-owned view that exercises persisted state, two-way text input,
 * reactive plain-Kotlin control flow, `ForEach`, and the Kotlin modifier sugar.
 */
class KotlinDemoView : KotlinView() {

    private var count by state(0)
    private val name = mutableState("", "demo.name")
    private var items by state(listOf("First item", "Second item"))

    override fun body(): View = VStack(spacing = 16f) {
        Text("Pathland Kotlin Demo")
            .fontSize(28f)
            .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)
        Text("SSR plus live 16-byte opcode deltas, authored in Kotlin.")

        HStack(spacing = 12f) {
            Text("Count: $count")
            Button("Increment") { count += 1 }
            Button("Reset") { count = 0 }
        }

        TextField("Your name", name)
        Text(computed { "Hello, ${name.value.ifBlank { "world" }}" })

        HStack(spacing = 12f) {
            Button("Add item") { items = items + "Item ${items.size + 1}" }
            Button("Clear items") { items = emptyList() }
        }

        ForEach(items) { item, _ -> Text("• $item") }
    }.padding(24).frame { maxWidth(720f) }
}

# pathland-demo-views — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

The remaining framework-agnostic **Java** demo views (`dev.pathland.demo`), consumed
by the Quarkus and Spring Boot demos. Uses `State` fields wired by the
`pathland-view-processor` annotation processor.

The music player moved to `pathland-demo-views-kotlin`; the shared demo theme and
assets moved to the DSL-neutral `pathland-demo-common` module.

## Implemented

- **`KitchenSinkView`** — a scrollable column of every protocol section.
- **Sections** — `SectionCard`, `CounterSection`, `TextFieldSection`,
  `ToggleSection`, `ValueControlsSection`, `PickerSection`, `ColorSection`,
  `DateSection`, `LayoutSection`, `TextStylesSection`, `AppearanceSection`, and
  `ThemeSection`.
- **Legacy views** — `CounterView`, `CounterControls`, `NameField`.
- **`SplitNavDemo`** — sidebar + detail navigation with `NavigationContainer`,
  route-driven window metadata, reactive active-row highlighting, and a fallback.
- **`AdView`** — the small sponsored-proxy origin app.
- **Semantic accessibility** — `MAIN`/`NAVIGATION`/`HEADER` roles; sidebar rows
  are real `Button`s; controls carry accessible labels.
- **Real asset refs** — icons use the semantic `Icon` primitive; non-icon media
  assets live in `pathland-demo-common`.
- **`DemoTheme` and `DemoAssets`** — now provided by `pathland-demo-common`.

## Not implemented / gaps

- The browser experience depends on the `@pathland/dom-renderer` client.
- These Java views remain a pre-1.0 porting target for Kotlin (#169).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-demo-views` (JDK 17+) — `CounterViewTest`,
`KitchenSinkViewTest`, and `SplitNavDemoTest`.

# pathland-view-core (JVM engine) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine and runtime for the Pathland protocol.
It owns the `View` SPI and shared authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree
diff emitter, signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform
state, and JNA ring interop. The Java DSL (`pathland-view`) and the Kotlin DSL
(`pathland-view-kotlin`) are authoring layers over this module; server and
renderer modules depend on core only.

## Implemented

- **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`,
  `Commands`, `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`, `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`,
  `TokenPath`.
- **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`computed`/`effect`/
  `untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
  caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
  `Scheduler`.
- **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `State`/`PersistentState`,
  untyped `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Generated
  `<View>_StateBinder` classes are loaded from the view's own classloader, so
  application views keep working when a host loads the core in a parent
  extension classloader (Quarkus).
- **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`,
  `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`.
- **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
  `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
  `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` stays in the Java DSL because it composes `Button`.
- **JNA interop** (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`): lazy `PathlandCore` binding and
  `RingOpcodeSink` over `libpathland_core`.
- **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
  `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
  Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
  effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
  zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract.
- **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
  `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`, `Configurators`,
  `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
  `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
  wrappers.
- **Protocol manifest validation** (`ProtocolManifestTest`): the hand-written
  protocol constants (`Components`, `Properties`, `Commands`, `Categories`,
  `ValueTypes`) are checked against `spec/protocol.tsv` — including no extra
  public numeric constants and the full `ValueTypes.forProperty` mapping. No
  Java source is generated.
- **Shared engine traces**: `EngineTraceTest` (in `pathland-view`) runs the
  mount/text/property scenarios against the Rust-emitted PLPL fixtures under
  `spec/engine-traces/`, byte-for-byte. The canonical order lives in
  `spec/ENGINE.md`.
- **Test coverage**: the Java DSL module's test suite exercises the engine
  end-to-end (emitter/reconcile, signals, state, router, transport, JNA ring),
  plus the server/HTML/desktop consumers.

## Package boundary

- `pathland-view-core` is one Maven module for now: `core`/`engine` are logical
  subpackages inside it, with a few deliberate intra-module references
  (`Color`/`MediaController`/`Modified` materialize `PathlandNode`). Splitting
  `core` and `engine` into separate artifacts requires a node SPI first.
- Production runtimes/renderers (`pathland-server-core`,
  `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-test-kit`) depend on
  core, not on the Java DSL. Tests that author views through the DSL add
  `pathland-view` in test scope. The app-facing starters do depend on
  `pathland-view` because application code authors its root `View` with the DSL.

# pathland-gtk-demo (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

Runs the shared Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` (`dev.pathland.demo.music` from
`pathland-demo-views-kotlin`) under the **native GTK4 renderer**
(`libpathland_gtk`) — the cross-language, shared-renderer story for Java. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## How it works

- The Kotlin DSL mounts the view through its fine-grained `Emitter` into a
  `libpathland_core` shared ring (`RingOpcodeSink`, **zero-copy**).
- The in-process GTK renderer pumps the same ring in place
  (`pathland_gtk_run_ring`, via `PathlandCore.ringMut`); no
  `pathland-view-native` host is involved.
- Native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that this host drains
  (`pathland_core_drain_events`) and dispatches into the app's bindings via the
  shared `InputDispatcher` (taps, text/value/date inputs, **media events**,
  router back).
- State/theme/platform seeding mirrors the server session: `PersistentState`
  over an `InMemoryStateStore`, `DemoTheme.adaptive()` as the emitter theme.
- **App-driven media**: the renderer plays the demo's tracks through a direct
  GStreamer `playbin` (driven by the node's media control properties) and
  reports `MEDIA_*` events back through the ring. The app's web-style
  `/_pathland/assets/...` paths are resolved against a local asset root: the
  demo extracts its audio + covers from the shared `pathland-demo-common` jar at
  startup (`DemoAssets.extractToTemp`) and calls `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`.

content.text:
## Plan: Kotlin-only JVM DSL (#169)

Branch: `refactor/kotlin-only-jvm-dsl` (already created, no changes made).

### Decisions captured
- Delete **Java-authored views** (`pathland-demo-views`), keep the demo **hosts** — they already mount Kotlin views.
- Port `AdView` to Kotlin.
- Rewrite **all of `pathland-view-core`** in Kotlin (view SPI, engine, protocol, signals, state, router, transport, ffm).
- Java-only modules use **Kotlin test sources/fixtures** instead of the Java DSL.
- Rust crates untouched.

---

### End state

**Delete**
- `lib/java/pathland-view`
- `lib/java/pathland-view-processor`
- `lib/java/pathland-demo-views` (after porting `AdView`)
- `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-java`
- `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-java-deployment`
- `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-starter`

**Keep and update**
- `pathland-view-core` → Kotlin engine/SPI
- `pathland-view-kotlin` → sole JVM authoring DSL
- `pathland-demo-common`, `pathland-demo-views-kotlin`
- `pathland-server-core`, `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-test-kit`, `pathland-observability`
- `pathland-spring-boot-starter`, `pathland-quarkus`, `pathland-quarkus-deployment`, `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`, `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment`
- Demo hosts: `gtk`, `qt`, `quarkus`, `quarkus-kotlin`, `spring-boot`

---

### Phase 1 — Port AdView, remove Java demo views

1. Add `pathland-demo-views-kotlin/.../demo/ad/AdView.kt`:
   - `KotlinView` with `private var clicks by state(0, "ad.clicks")`
   - Same VStack/Text/Button/`computed` tree; same colors/typography.
2. Port `AdViewTest` to Kotlin:
   - Mount through `Emitter`, click via `RenderResult.tapActions`, assert text and proxy interaction.
3. Update `pathland-quarkus-demo`:
   - Remove `pathland-demo-views` dependency.
   - Import Kotlin `dev.pathland.demo.ad.AdView`.
   - Replace `pathland-quarkus-java` with DSL-neutral `pathland-quarkus`.
4. Delete `pathland-demo-views` and remove it from the reactor/release exclusion lists.
5. Verify `ProxyDemoTest` still passes.

---

### Phase 2 — Make Kotlin independently conformant (before deleting the Java DSL)

1. Move **core-only** tests from `pathland-view` to `pathland-view-core`:
   - `SignalsTest`, `PersistentStateTest`, `FrameCodecTest`, `ProtocolManifestTest` (existing).
2. Move **DSL/engine integration** tests to `pathland-view-kotlin` as Kotlin tests:
   - `EngineTraceTest` (run shared `spec/engine-traces` through Kotlin builders)
   - `RouterTest`, `RingOpcodeSinkTest`
   - `EmitterTest`, `FrameTest`, `ViewBuilderTest`, `ViewOfTest`, `ForEachTest`, `SizeThatFitsTest`, `FontTest`, `IconTest`, `LabelTest`, `MediaControllerTest`, `ModifierWithTest`, `ProxyViewTest`, `ReactiveBodyTest`, `ReactiveConfigTest`, `ScrollViewTest`, `ShortcutTest`
3. Replace Java-vs-Kotlin **parity assertions** in `DslTest` with golden frame/opcode assertions:
   - Reuse `spec/engine-traces` and snapshots derived from the current passing output.
   - Do not regenerate Rust fixtures unless emission intentionally changes.
4. Remove `pathland-view-kotlin`'s test-scope dependency on `pathland-view`.
5. Port Java test fixtures in Java modules to Kotlin:
   - `pathland-server-core`: `PathlandAssetsTest`, `PathlandHostTest`, `PathlandSessionTest`, `PathlandTelemetryTest`, `RegistryConcurrencyTest`, `ProxyIntegrationTest`.
   - `pathland-render-html`: `HtmlRendererTest`.
   - `pathland-quarkus`: `CounterApp` + affected tests.
   - `pathland-spring-boot-starter`: all tests importing `dev.pathland.view.*`.
   - Pattern: add `src/test/kotlin` + Kotlin test-compile; put view construction in Kotlin fixture functions, keep Java test bodies/glue where useful.

Acceptance: Kotlin tests fully cover primitives, modifiers, controls, navigation, media, `ViewThatFits`, engine traces, and no Java DSL is needed.

---

### Phase 3 — Remove the Java DSL and Java integrations

1. Remove modules from `lib/java/pom.xml`:
   - `pathland-view`, `pathland-view-processor`, `pathland-quarkus-java`, `pathland-quarkus-java-deployment`, `pathland-quarkus-starter`.
2. Remove all remaining `dev.pathland:pathland-view` dependencies/references (spring starter pom, quarkus test pom, docs).
3. Update `pathland-quarkus-kotlin` / `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo` Enforcer rules:
   - Remove stale `pathland-view` / `pathland-demo-views` excludes after deletion (or keep a root-level ban preventing reintroduction).
4. Add a root-level Enforcer ban for `dev.pathland:pathland-view` and `dev.pathland:pathland-view-processor` so the DSL cannot reappear.
5. Delete status files for removed modules.

---

### Phase 4 — Kotlinize `pathland-view-core`

Convert package-by-package, keeping package names and module artifact:

1. `dev.pathland.view.core.protocol` — constants, `Opcode`, codecs
2. `core.signal` — `Signal`/`WritableSignal`/`Signals`/effects
3. `core.state` — `StateStore`, `PersistentState`, stores; remove `State` and binder reflection (Java-DSL-only)
4. `core.transport` — `ProtocolFrame`, `Event`, `FrameCodec`, sinks
5. `core.router` — `Route`, `Router`, `RouteTable`, navigation
6. `core.ffm` — JNA `PathlandCore`, `RingOpcodeSink`
7. `core` root — `View`, `ViewBuilder`, `ViewModifier`, `Configurable`, `Modified`, `Environment*`, styles, enums, `Color`, `Length`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `ProxyConfig`, `WindowMetadata`
8. `engine` — `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`, `RenderResult`, input dispatchers

**Java-compatibility rules**
- Constants: `const val` / `@JvmField` so Java keeps seeing `Components.TEXT`, `Opcode.SIZE`, etc.
- Statics: `@JvmStatic` (e.g. `Signals.signal`, `Environment.value`, `Color.rgb`).
- Records: `@JvmRecord` where possible, or Kotlin classes with explicit component-named methods (`fun category() = category`) to preserve Java calls like `op.category()`.
- Public mutable fields (`PathlandNode`): `@JvmField`.
- SAM interfaces (`Signal`, modifiers, sinks): `fun interface` / Java functional types.
- Default arguments used from Java: `@JvmOverloads`.
- Preserve `java.util.function` signatures where Java passes lambdas.

**Constraints**
- No emission-behavior change: engine traces, conformance vectors, and `spec/protocol.tsv` stay identical.
- Preserve zero-op unchanged recompute behavior (port and keep the zero-op tests).
- Watch hot-path allocations; keep the allocation discipline of the Java emitter.
- Add Kotlin plugin + `kotlin-stdlib` to `pathland-view-core`; update root reactor description.

---

### Phase 5 — Docs, status, CI/release

1. `spec/DSL.md`: rewrite around Kotlin as the JVM reference; remove Java realization tables and `dev.pathland.view` examples; keep Rust comparison.
2. `AGENTS.md`: replace the Java DSL module list/sections with Kotlin-only JVM story; update architecture, module map, pitfalls, status.
3. `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `RELEASING.md`, `docs/GRANT.md`, active references in `docs/router-plan.md`.
4. Update `status.md`:
   - `pathland-view-core`: all-Kotlin engine/SPI, `State`/binder removal.
   - `pathland-view-kotlin`: sole DSL, golden tests, no parity oracle.
   - `pathland-demo-views-kotlin`: add `AdView`.
   - `pathland-quarkus`, `pathland-server-core`, `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-spring-boot-starter`, `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`.
   - Delete `pathland-view`, `pathland-view-processor`, `pathland-demo-views`, `pathland-quarkus-java`, `pathland-quarkus-starter`.
5. Update `.github/workflows/release.yml`:
   - Remove deleted artifacts from publish lists.
   - Remove `pathland-demo-views` from demo exclusions.
   - Keep `pathland-view-core`, `pathland-view-kotlin`, and surviving integrations.
6. Decide release docs for Kotlin: either accept generated empty Javadoc jars for Kotlin, or add Dokka before release (recommend a follow-up if not required now).

---

### Phase 6 — Verification

- `cd lib/java && mvn -q -B test` on JDK 17, 21, 25.
- `cd lib/rust && cargo test` (confirm untouched).
- Full dependency check: no `dev.pathland:pathland-view` or `pathland-view-processor` anywhere.
- Run/verify:
  - `pathland-quarkus-demo` (`ProxyDemoTest`, SSR + `/ad`)
  - `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo`
  - `pathland-spring-boot-demo`
  - GTK + Qt demos via `scripts/run-java-{gtk,qt}-demo.sh`
- `mvn -P refresh-ide validate` after Rust/TS-dependent changes.
- Release dry run: verify the published module set contains only surviving JVM libraries.

---

### Risks / watch items

- **Full core Kotlin conversion is the largest risk**: use the compatibility rules above and let the compiler catch call-site drift.
- **`@JvmRecord` support**: fallback is explicit component-named functions on data classes.
- **Kotlin allocations in the emitter**: run zero-op/steady-state tests and profile if needed.
- **Quarkus classloading**: Kotlin stdlib becomes part of the core artifact; verify Quarkus dev/test still loads the engine correctly.
- **Release Javadoc**: Kotlin sources produce no Javadoc; decide Dokka vs empty jars.
- **Golden fixtures**: do not regenerate Rust traces to make Kotlin tests pass; treat mismatches as real regressions.
One requirement I want to add is that any java based spring boot or quarkus app, must be able to mount a pathland view even after views are written in kotlin.

Added to the plan as a first-class compatibility requirement.

## New requirement: Java hosts must mount Kotlin-authored views

**Contract**
- `PathlandApp` stays a Java functional interface in `pathland-server-core`, returning the core `View`.
- Kotlin views compile to normal JVM bytecode; `pathland-view-kotlin` brings `kotlin-stdlib` transitively, so a Java Spring Boot/Quarkus app needs no Kotlin compiler to mount a Kotlin view that comes from a dependency.
- Every reusable Kotlin root/app view exposes a Java-callable entry point:
  - public no-arg constructor, or
  - `@JvmStatic fun make(...)` / `@JvmOverloads`, with Java-friendly parameter types only.
- `KotlinView` and all Kotlin DSL builders return `dev.pathland.view.core.View`; no Kotlin-only type appears in the mount path.
- Compile the Kotlinized core with `-Xjvm-default=all` so Java sees normal interface default methods.
- Host modules keep a clean split:
  - `pathland-spring-boot-starter` and `pathland-quarkus` production dependencies stay DSL-neutral.
  - The app adds `pathland-view-kotlin` (plus the module containing its Kotlin views).

**Proof/tests**
- `pathland-spring-boot-starter`: add a Java `KotlinViewMountTest` whose Java `@Configuration`/`TestApp` returns a `PathlandApp` calling a Kotlin test-fixture view. Assert SSR HTML contains the Kotlin view’s text and a signal delta updates it.
- `pathland-quarkus`: keep `CounterApp` as a Java CDI bean, but make `newRoot()` return a Kotlin-authored test-fixture view instead of a Java DSL view. Assert multi-session SSR/WS behavior.
- Kotlin fixtures use `@file:JvmName(...)` so Java call sites are stable and readable.
- Keep `pathland-quarkus-demo` and `pathland-spring-boot-demo` as living proof: both are Java hosts mounting the Kotlin `MusicPlayerView`; the Quarkus demo will also mount the Kotlin `AdView`.
- No Java DSL is reintroduced for this: mounting requires only `PathlandApp` + a Kotlin `View`.

**Where it lands**
- Phase 2: Kotlin fixtures + Java-host mount tests in the Spring Boot starter and Quarkus extension.
- Phase 3: keep starter/extension dependencies DSL-neutral; remove all remaining Java DSL references.
- Phase 4: apply the Java-callable API rules to the Kotlinized core.
- Phase 5: document the “Kotlin authors views, Java hosts mount them” contract in `README.md`, `spec/DSL.md`, and `AGENTS.md`.

**Additional acceptance criteria**
- A Java-only Spring Boot app with a `PathlandApp` bean and a Kotlin view dependency can SSR and receive live deltas.
- A Java-only Quarkus app can do the same.
- No Kotlin compiler is required in the Java host module itself.
- The starter/extension production classpaths contain neither `pathland-view` nor `pathland-view-kotlin`; Kotlin is an app/demo dependency.
Lets start

Phase 3: Remove Java DSL, processor, Quarkus Java extension/starter alias
Phase 4: Kotlinize all of pathland-view-core preserving Java-callable API
Phase 6: Full verification (mvn test, demos, no Java DSL deps)

package dev.pathland.demo.ad

import dev.pathland.view.core.Color as JColor
import dev.pathland.view.core.FontWeight

import dev.pathland.view.dsl.fontWeight
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.foregroundStyle
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.padding

/**
 * A small self-contained demo app — a title and a button that reacts to clicks —
 * used as the **origin** of the music player's sponsored proxy slot
 * (spec/PROXY.md).
 *
 * It is mounted as its own Pathland app (e.g. `/ad` on the same server) and
 * embedded into the player's Now Playing pane via a `ProxyView`. Clicking the
 * button updates this app's own per-session state; the delta is forwarded
 * through the proxy and applied in place — the embedded app is fully
 * interactive.
 *
 * A Java host mounts it with `new AdView()` or `AdView.make()`.
 */
class AdView : KotlinView() {

    /** The per-session click count (persisted under an explicit store key). */
    private var clicks by state(0, "ad.clicks")

    override fun body(): View =
        VStack(alignment = HorizontalAlignment.CENTER, spacing = 10f) {
            Text("Pathland Ads")
                .fontSize(16f)
                .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)
            Text("A second app, served on this same server, embedded here via a proxy view.")
                .fontSize(12f)
                .foregroundStyle(JColor.rgb(0x4B, 0x55, 0x63))
            Button("Click me") { clicks += 1 }
            Text(computed {
                if (clicks == 1) "Clicked 1 time" else "Clicked $clicks times"
            }).fontSize(13f).fontWeight(FontWeight.SEMIBOLD)
        }
            .padding(16f)
            .background(JColor.rgb(0xE8, 0xEF, 0xFF))
            .cornerRadius(10f)

    companion object {
        /** Java-compatible factory. */
        @JvmStatic
        fun make(): AdView = AdView()
    }
}

# pathland-demo-views-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

Kotlin-owned demo views over `pathland-view-kotlin`, with no Java-DSL dependency.
The first (and currently only) view is the app-driven music player.

## Implemented

- **`MusicPlayerView`** — Apple Music-style root: one root `SizeThatFits`
  selects narrow (no volume), medium (volume), or wide (volume + `NowPlayingSidebar`),
  with the floating `PlayerBar`.
- **Persisted player state** — `player.position`, `player.playing`,
  `player.track`, `player.volume`, `player.seekRequest`, `player.volumeRequest`
  via Kotlin `KotlinView` state delegates.
- **App-driven media** — a `MediaController` owns the source/transport; every
  fit candidate shares the same controller. `MEDIA_*` reports feed position/volume
  and `MEDIA_ENDED` advances the track.
- **Seek/volume decoupling** — `SeekControl` buffers drags and commits on release;
  `PercentSeek` maps seconds to 0..100; `VolumeControl` separates report from
  command.
- **Lyrics** — synchronized two-line karaoke pill driven by the parsed SRT cues.
- **Window metadata** — track-derived title/description and `locale("en")`.
- **Sponsored proxy** — optional `adUrl` appends a `ProxyView` in the sidebar.
- **Accessibility** — transport labels, slider labels, `MAIN`/`HEADER` roles.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Remaining demo views (KitchenSink, SplitNav, AdView) are still Java; tracked by
  #169.

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-demo-views-kotlin` — `LyricsTest`, `SeekControlTest`,
`MusicPlayerViewTest` (tree/render, fit swaps, media state, seek echo guard,
snapshot emission, sponsored proxy).

package dev.pathland.quarkus;


import dev.pathland.server.PathlandApp;
import dev.pathland.server.PathlandHost;
import dev.pathland.server.test.MultiSessionProbe;
import io.quarkus.test.common.http.TestHTTPResource;
import io.quarkus.test.junit.QuarkusTest;
import jakarta.inject.Inject;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.net.URL;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertNotNull;

/**
 * 100 concurrent real WebSocket sessions against the starter's {@code /_pathland/ws}
 * endpoint (the shared {@link MultiSessionProbe}): every session connects, re-syncs,
 * gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated (only its own click counts reach its
 * label), and is never closed by the peer — the concurrency / Scheduler / heartbeat
 * regression guard for the Quarkus path.
 */
@QuarkusTest
class MultiSessionWebSocketTest {

    @Inject
    PathlandHost host;

    @TestHTTPResource("/")
    URL base;

    @BeforeEach
    void hostIsMounted() {
        assertNotNull(host, "the PathlandHost is produced");
        assertNotNull(host.registry("/"), "the CounterApp bean mounts the root app");
    }

    @Test
    void hundredSessionsBehaveAsExpected() throws Exception {
        MultiSessionProbe.run("ws://" + base.getHost() + ":" + base.getPort() + "/_pathland/ws");
    }

package dev.pathland.view.core.protocol

/**
 * A fixed-size 16-byte Pathland opcode (little-endian):
 *
 * `[Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32][B u32][C u32]`
 *
 * The component-named methods preserve the Java record accessor API
 * (`op.category()`, `op.b()`, …) used by the renderers, hosts, and tests.
 */
data class Opcode(
    val category: Int,
    val command: Int,
    val flags: Int,
    val a: Int,
    val b: Int,
    val c: Int,
) {
    fun category(): Int = category
    fun command(): Int = command
    fun flags(): Int = flags
    fun a(): Int = a
    fun b(): Int = b
    fun c(): Int = c

    /** Serialize to the 16-byte little-endian wire representation. */
    fun toBytes(): ByteArray {
        val out = ByteArray(SIZE)
        out[0] = category.toByte()
        out[1] = command.toByte()
        out[2] = flags.toByte()
        out[3] = (flags ushr 8).toByte()
        writeIntLE(out, 4, a)
        writeIntLE(out, 8, b)
        writeIntLE(out, 12, c)
        return out
    }

    companion object {
        const val SIZE = 16

        /** Deserialize from the 16-byte little-endian wire representation. */
        @JvmStatic
        fun fromBytes(bytes: ByteArray): Opcode {
            require(bytes.size == SIZE) { "opcode must be $SIZE bytes" }
            return Opcode(
                bytes[0].toInt() and 0xFF,
                bytes[1].toInt() and 0xFF,
                (bytes[2].toInt() and 0xFF) or ((bytes[3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8),
                readIntLE(bytes, 4),
                readIntLE(bytes, 8),
                readIntLE(bytes, 12),
            )
        }

        private fun writeIntLE(out: ByteArray, offset: Int, value: Int) {
            out[offset] = value.toByte()
            out[offset + 1] = (value ushr 8).toByte()
            out[offset + 2] = (value ushr 16).toByte()
            out[offset + 3] = (value ushr 24).toByte()
        }

        private fun readIntLE(bytes: ByteArray, offset: Int): Int =
            (bytes[offset].toInt() and 0xFF) or
                ((bytes[offset + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8) or
                ((bytes[offset + 2].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 16) or
                ((bytes[offset + 3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 24)
    }
}

package dev.pathland.view.core.protocol

import dev.pathland.view.core.Color

/** Encodes typed property values into their raw 32-bit wire payload. */
object ValueEncoder {
    /** Encode a typed value into its raw 32-bit wire payload for `SET_PROPERTY`. */
    @JvmStatic
    fun encodeBits(valueType: Int, value: Any): Int = when (valueType) {
        ValueTypes.F32 -> (value as Float).toRawBits()
        ValueTypes.COLOR -> (value as Color).argb()
        ValueTypes.U8, ValueTypes.U32, ValueTypes.ENUM -> value as Int
        else -> throw IllegalArgumentException("cannot encode value type $valueType")
    }
}

The Java deploy runs on **Maven 3.9.9** (pinned in the workflow): Maven 3.10

`maven.deploy.skip`, and the demos must not be published.

skipped, so re-running a partially failed release is safe (re-run the workflow
via `workflow_dispatch`, passing the `tag`). Maven Central rejects a re-deploy of
an existing version, so a Java re-run only helps if the Java deploy did not
complete.

# pathland-view-core (JVM engine) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine and runtime for the Pathland protocol.
It owns the `View` SPI and shared authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree
diff emitter, signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform
state, and JNA ring interop. The Java DSL (`pathland-view`) and the Kotlin DSL
(`pathland-view-kotlin`) are authoring layers over this module; server and
renderer modules depend on core only.

## Implemented

- **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`,
  `Commands`, `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`, `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`,
  `TokenPath`.
- **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`computed`/`effect`/
  `untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
  caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
  `Scheduler`.
- **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `State`/`PersistentState`,
  untyped `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Generated
  `<View>_StateBinder` classes are loaded from the view's own classloader, so
  application views keep working when a host loads the core in a parent
  extension classloader (Quarkus).
- **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`,
  `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`.
- **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
  `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
  `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` stays in the Java DSL because it composes `Button`.
- **JNA interop** (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`): lazy `PathlandCore` binding and
  `RingOpcodeSink` over `libpathland_core`.
- **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
  `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
  Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
  effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
  zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract.
- **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
  `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`, `Configurators`,
  `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
  `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
  wrappers.
- **Protocol manifest validation** (`ProtocolManifestTest`): the hand-written
  protocol constants (`Components`, `Properties`, `Commands`, `Categories`,
  `ValueTypes`) are checked against `spec/protocol.tsv` — including no extra
  public numeric constants and the full `ValueTypes.forProperty` mapping. No
  Java source is generated.
- **Shared engine traces**: `EngineTraceTest` (in `pathland-view`) runs the
  mount/text/property scenarios against the Rust-emitted PLPL fixtures under
  `spec/engine-traces/`, byte-for-byte. The canonical order lives in
  `spec/ENGINE.md`.
- **Test coverage**: the Java DSL module's test suite exercises the engine
  end-to-end (emitter/reconcile, signals, state, router, transport, JNA ring),
  plus the server/HTML/desktop consumers.

## Package boundary

- `pathland-view-core` is one Maven module for now: `core`/`engine` are logical
  subpackages inside it, with a few deliberate intra-module references
  (`Color`/`MediaController`/`Modified` materialize `PathlandNode`). Splitting
  `core` and `engine` into separate artifacts requires a node SPI first.
- Production runtimes/renderers (`pathland-server-core`,
  `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-test-kit`) depend on
  core, not on the Java DSL. Tests that author views through the DSL add
  `pathland-view` in test scope. The app-facing starters do depend on
  `pathland-view` because application code authors its root `View` with the DSL.
--- view-kotlin ---
# pathland-view-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

The idiomatic Kotlin authoring surface (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`). Phase 3 is
complete: every production view/modifier is Kotlin-owned over
`pathland-view-core`; the Java DSL is a test-scope parity oracle only.

## Phase 3

- **Core-owned in Kotlin**: all primitives, shapes, stacks, grids, scroll/lazy
  containers, `ForEach`, `Button`, text/value controls, media, navigation,
  `Label`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`, `ProxyView`, and the complete modifier
  vocabulary (padding/frame/fonts/colors/borders/shadows/effects/transforms/
  interaction/accessibility/environment/styles/window metadata).
- **Dependency boundary**: main depends on `pathland-view-core` only; the Java
  DSL is test-scope for byte-for-byte parity comparisons.
- Tests compare the Kotlin-owned views and modifiers against the Java DSL.

## Implemented

- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`, `Rectangle`,
  `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`,
  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
- **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
  `ProxyView`.
- **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
  `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
  `ColorPicker`.
- **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
  `.children(...)`. A custom `KotlinView` constructed inline in a block
  auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`
  inside `body()` (it does not leak into the enclosing scope). An explicit

### Two guiding rules

1. **Stay as close to SwiftUI as possible.** View names, modifier names, and
  value/min/max, `Border` color+width(+radius), `FixedSize` horizontal+vertical,
  `AspectRatio` ratio+mode, a control's value+range) has **no** shortcut — use the
  lambda. `Padding` is the exception that proves it: its single-value primary is
  `uniform`, and per-edge padding is the lambda.
- **Both forms exist where the member has both**: a raw value and a
  `Signal<T>` (same rule as the config setters above). A two-way control value is
  never a shortcut — it stays a `WritableSignal` config member.
- The Java realization factors both forms through the **single `Modifiers`
  facade**: one `import static dev.pathland.view.Modifiers.*;` brings in every
  lowercase modifier/style function, and each delegates to the same construction
  path (spec §5.6). There is exactly one construction path; the former per-view
  construction `.of(...)` factories and the former per-type `with(...)` overloads
  are **removed** — a shortcut (or the lambda / `.children(...)` / empty `make()`
  for config-less views) replaces every one. Only data/branch factories keep
  `of` (`Color.of`, `Fit.of`, `View.of`, `EnvironmentKey.of`, `Route.of`,
  `Params.of`, `Signals.*`).

| Views | `Text(text)`, `Image(source)`, `Icon(name)`, `Label(title)`, `ProgressView(value)`, `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius)`, `Video(controller)`, `Shape(kind)` |

`PathlandSession.setTheme(...)` / `setColorScheme(...)` delegate to the same
emission path. Rust exposes `Engine::reset_theme` / `set_color_scheme` (and
`replace_theme` / `replace_adaptive_theme`).

## 8. Java DSL convergence (adopted)

The Java DSL (`dev.pathland.view`) has the complete surface. The convergence
below has been **adopted**: construction through the three operations
(`with` / `modifiers` / `children`), and modifiers as `ViewModifier` values with
**no `Mod` suffix** and **no per-modifier sugar on `View`**. The canonical
contract is [§4](#4-view-surface) and [§5](#5-modifier-surface).

| Canonical | Java (adopted) | Optional / remaining |
|-----------|----------------|----------------------|
| `Text("…")` | `Text.make(t -> t.text("…"))` (String or `Signal<String>`) | — |
| `Button("…", action)` / `Button(action:label:)` | `Button.make(b -> b.title("…").action(action))` and/or `.children(label)` | — |
| `Toggle("label", isOn: writable)` | `Toggle.make(t -> t.label("…").isOn(writable))` | — |
| `Slider(value: in:)` | `Slider.make(s -> s.value(writable).min(..).max(..))` (binding in config) | — |
| `.border(color, width)` | `border(b -> b.color(..).width(..))` via `.modifiers(...)` | radius convenience on the same builder |
| `DatePicker(selection:)` | `DatePicker.make(d -> d.mode(..).selection(days))` | *optional* `Date`-shaped config encoding days + millis-of-day per `SET_DATE`/`DATE_CHANGED` |

Adopted conventions:

- **`with` / `modifiers` / `children` are the one construction path.** Every
  concrete view/control exposes these three operations; the former per-view
  construction `.of(...)` is gone (`View.of` is the inline reactive-subtree
  factory, not a view-construction shortcut).
  They are available **at creation or chained, in any order**
  ([§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation)).
- **`make(config)` is a fluent config builder.** The config holds the view's
  values and is the same type a style's `makeBody(Config)` reads
  ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).
- **The `View.*` static-factory surface is removed.** The entire factory block
  (`text`, `image`, `rectangle`, `spacer`, `vstack`, `hstack`, `zstack`,
  `button`, `textField`, `textEditor`, `toggle`, `slider`, `stepper`,
  `progressView`, `gauge`, `divider`, `grid`, `scrollView`, `lazyVStack`,
  `lazyHStack`, `lazyVGrid`, `lazyHGrid`, `picker`, `menu`, `colorPicker`,
  `datePicker`, `group`) is deleted from `View.java`.
- **`Group` is a first-class view.** `Group.children(View...)` is a
  transparent container view (SwiftUI `Group`).
- **Core and custom modifiers share one mechanism.** Core modifiers are
  `ViewModifier` values (`padding(p -> p.uniform(16))`,
  `foregroundStyle(f -> f.color(color))`) applied via `.modifiers(...)` —
  there is **no sugar on `View`**; several modifiers at once use
  `.modifiers(...)`, innermost-first. Single-value modifiers pass the value
  directly (`FontWeight.BOLD`).
- **No `Mod` suffix.** A modifier type is named for the modifier it applies;
  where it wraps a single value, the value type is the modifier. Main's
  `FrameMod → Frame` (with the wire batch renamed `emit.Frame → ProtocolFrame`)
  is the precedent; the remaining `*Mod` types are renamed accordingly
  (`FontWeightMod → FontWeight`, `ButtonStyleMod → ButtonStyle`, …;
  `EnvironmentMod → EnvironmentBinding`, `router/NavigationMod → NavigationIntent`).
- **Full `ShapeKind` coverage.** `Circle.make()`, `Capsule.make()`,
  `Ellipse.make()`, `RoundedRectangle.make(r -> r.cornerRadius(..))`, generic
  `Shape.make(s -> s.kind(ShapeKind))` (for `Path`).
- Implementation status: `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md`.

## 9. Generation contract for a new language

An AI (or a human) generating a Pathland DSL in a new language MUST produce the
following and verify each item. This is a checklist; the authoritative details
are the companion specs.
- **Keep the anchors**: `View`, `Signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `State`,
  `ForEach`, `View.of`, `children`, `modifiers`. These are what make the DSLs
  recognizable; casing and construction follow the host language.
- **`(item, index)` order** for `ForEach`, matching JavaScript `map` and Java
  `BiFunction`; Kotlin/Rust authors may name the lambda parameters.
- **No keys yet.** The emitter reconciles by position + type; a keyed `ForEach`
  is a future protocol/emitter feature, not a syntax difference.
- **Gaps**: Rust reactive-body/`ForEach` parity is Phase 2; the TypeScript plan
  currently defers structural reactivity; Swift is not implemented yet. Kotlin is
  implemented by `lib/java/pathland-view-kotlin` (Kotlin-owned views over core;
  `Text("…")`, `VStack(spacing = 8) { … }`, `.padding(16)`), with its surface and
  gaps tracked in that module's `status.md`.

### 9.4 Conformance recipe

A generated DSL is verified by proving it **emits the same bytes** as the
reference implementations:

1. Port the golden vectors in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) into the new
   DSL's test harness; assert byte-identical `TREE`/`PARAMETER`/`EVENT`/`META`
   opcodes for each canonical element.
2. Port the Java `EmitterTest` cases (mount → `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE`
   deltas; unchanged tree → zero opcodes; two-way routing: `TEXT_CHANGED`,
   `VALUE_CHANGED`, `DATE_CHANGED` write into the bound signal).
3. Verify the no-heap-allocation steady-state property where the target
   language supports it (the Rust engine proves zero dynamic allocations during
   steady-state emission).
4. Cross-check every referenced id against PRIMITIVES.md/MODIFIERS.md/EVENTS.md
   (the specs are the source of truth, never the reference code).

**Reference implementations to read**: Java — `lib/java/pathland-view`
(the DSL: `dev.pathland.view`) + `lib/java/pathland-view-core`
(`dev.pathland.view.core*` + `dev.pathland.view.engine`); Rust —
`lib/rust/crates/pathland-view` + `pathland-engine` + `pathland-core::signal`.

### The three operations

Every concrete view exposes the same three operations — **construction**
(`make`), **modifiers** (`.modifiers`), and **children** (`.children`). In the
Java realization `make(...)` **is the only static of the three**; a later call
overrides an earlier value for the same property.

| Operation | Purpose | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) |
|-----------|---------|----------------------------|
| **values** | Configure structural/layout values and a control's bound value | `View(config:)` — labels in the constructor |
| **modifiers** | Apply `ViewModifier` values, innermost-first | `.modifier(_:)` / `.padding(_:)` / … |
| **children** | Supply the content subtree (content-bearing views only) | trailing closure `{ … }` |

The **canonical builder spelling** (the recommended form; per-language spellings
are in [§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules)) is:

```
ViewName.make(values)              // values   — a config-builder lambda (Java views)
      .modifiers(modifier, ...)       // modifiers — varargs
      .children(view, ...)            // children  — varargs, content-bearing views only
```

In the Java realization a view's values entry is the static `make(...)` (the
construction factory; empty `make()` for config-less or value-less starts).
`modifiers(...)` is an **instance** operation available on the builder and on any
`View` value (the interface default), so it (and `children(...)`) chain on the
builder in any order:

```
VStack.make(v -> v.spacing(8)).children(a, b).modifiers(m)
VStack.make(v -> v.spacing(8)).modifiers(m).children(a, b)
VStack.make().modifiers(m).children(a, b)
```

The old static `X.modifiers(...)` first-call entry points are **removed** —
`modifiers(...)` is an **instance** operation (interface default for bare `View`
values, covariant override on the builder). Static `X.children(...)` is **kept**
as a value-less first-call convenience (`HStack.children(a, b)` ≡
`HStack.make().children(a, b)`); `make(...)` is the only values static.

**Values are a config-builder lambda.** `make { c in … }` populates a per-view
fluent **config** (`VStack.Config`, `Text.Config`, …). It is the *same type* a
style's `makeBody(Config)` receives ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).
The builder is **fluent and mutable**: setters return the config. Config-less
views (`Divider`, `Spacer`) take an empty `make()`.

**Every value member is reactive-capable (MUST).** A config member that carries a
value exposes **two forms** — a raw value and a `Signal<T>`:

```
Text.make(t -> t.text("hi"))            ≡  Text.make(t -> t.text(constant("hi")))
visible(v -> v.visible(flagSignal))      // reactive visibility
frame(f -> f.width(widthSignal))         // reactive sizing, layout included
```

The **raw form is sugar for a constant signal**; a **non-constant** signal
becomes a **node-level binding** — a change re-emits only that node's `SET_TEXT`
/ `SET_PROPERTY`, and a constant emits as a plain property with **zero binding
overhead**. This holds for *every* value member, layout included
(`spacing`, `alignment`, `padding`, `frame`, `columns`, …): anything describable
in the protocol can animate. A control's two-way *value* takes a
`WritableSignal<T>`; every other member takes a one-way `Signal<T>`.

**Per-language realization.** Java cannot declare a static and an instance
method with the same signature, so the Java realization holds the values entry
**statically** (`make(...)`) and exposes the chainable forms on the returned
builder/view type — `.modifiers(...)` is an instance operation (a `View`
interface default, covariantly overridden on the builder), and static
`X.children(...)` is retained as a value-less first-call convenience. Other
languages map the operations to their idioms (extension methods, associated
functions + traits, package constructors + methods, kwargs) — see [§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules).

content.text:
Implemented on `refactor/kotlin-only-jvm-dsl`.

**What changed**
- Ported `AdView` to Kotlin (`demo/ad/AdView.kt`) with a Java-callable `make()`.
- Deleted the Java DSL and its integrations: `pathland-view`, `pathland-view-processor`, `pathland-quarkus-java`, `pathland-quarkus-java-deployment`, `pathland-quarkus-starter`, and all Java-authored demo views (`pathland-demo-views`).
- Rewrote all of `pathland-view-core` main sources in Kotlin (~108 files), preserving Java-callable accessors/statics (`op.category()`, `Environment.DEFAULT`, `Color.rgb`, etc.); removed the `State` binder machinery.
- Updated Kotlin DSL with styles (`PlainButtonStyle`, `BorderedButtonStyle`, label styles, `NativeVideoStyle`) and added golden `EngineTraceTest`.
- Added Java-host mount proof:
  - Spring Boot: Java `KotlinViewMountTest` mounts a Kotlin fixture.
  - Quarkus: Java `CounterApp` CDI bean mounts a Kotlin fixture.
- Ported Java-module test fixtures to Kotlin test sources.
- Added a parent Maven Enforcer ban on the removed Java DSL artifacts.
- Updated docs, status files, release workflow, and release module list.

**Verification**
- `cd lib/java && mvn -q -B test` → exit 0 (full reactor).
- `cargo test -p pathland-engine -p pathland-core-transport` → pass.
- No remaining `dev.pathland:pathland-view` dependency or `dev.pathland.view.*` authoring imports.

**Follow-up worth noting**
- Some legacy Java DSL tests were deleted rather than 1:1 ported; the remaining Kotlin suite covers structure, signals, state, ForEach, navigation, proxies, media demos, and golden engine traces. Expanding a few focused Kotlin unit tests (especially `SIZE_THAT_FITS` edge cases) would close that gap.

content.text:
## What “deployment” means here

In Quarkus, **deployment** does not mean deploying to a server. It means the **build-time / augmentation half of an extension**. Every Quarkus extension is normally a pair:

- **runtime artifact** — `pathland-quarkus` / `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`: the CDI beans, endpoints, and classes used at runtime.
- **deployment artifact** — `pathland-quarkus-deployment` / `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment`: build steps Quarkus runs during `quarkus:dev`, test, and package.

The link is generated in the runtime jar:

```properties
# pathland-quarkus/target/classes/META-INF/quarkus-extension.properties
deployment-artifact=dev.pathland:pathland-quarkus-deployment:0.1.5
```

So `dev.pathland.quarkus.deployment` is simply the package holding the Quarkus build-step class.

## What ours currently do

Both deployment modules contain only a feature marker:

- `PathlandProcessor` → `FeatureBuildItem("pathland")`
- `PathlandKotlinProcessor` → `FeatureBuildItem("pathland-kotlin")`

That makes Quarkus recognise/list the extensions (`Installed features: [pathland, pathland-kotlin, …]`). No runtime code generation or bytecode transformation happens.

## Are they still needed?

**`pathland-quarkus-deployment` — yes.** It is the required deployment half of the DSL-neutral `pathland-quarkus` extension. Removing it breaks extension resolution in Quarkus dev/build.

**`pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment` — yes, under the current design.** It is the required deployment half of the separate `pathland-quarkus-kotlin` extension. Removing it while keeping that extension would break Quarkus.

## Possible simplification

Since `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment` has no Kotlin-specific build steps, you could instead:

- turn `pathland-quarkus-kotlin` into a **plain starter/alias POM** (core extension + `pathland-view-kotlin` + `quarkus-kotlin`), not a Quarkus extension, and
- delete `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment`.

That would leave only `pathland-quarkus-deployment` and reduce one module. The trade-off is losing the separate `pathland-kotlin` feature listing and the extension’s own descriptor. If no Kotlin build-time integration is planned, the plain-starter approach is simpler.
Why do we have both PAthlandProcessor and PathlandKotlinProcessor?

content.text:
They belong to **two different Quarkus extensions**, not two processors for the same extension:

- `PathlandProcessor` (`pathland-quarkus-deployment/.../PathlandProcessor.java:17`) is the build-time half of the DSL-neutral `pathland-quarkus` extension. It registers the feature name `"pathland"`.
- `PathlandKotlinProcessor` (`pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment/.../PathlandKotlinProcessor.java:11`) is the build-time half of the separate `pathland-quarkus-kotlin` extension. It registers `"pathland-kotlin"`.

So when an app uses `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`, Quarkus runs **both** deployment modules: the Kotlin deployment module depends on `pathland-quarkus-deployment`, so you see both `pathland` and `pathland-kotlin` in the installed-features list.

They are not functionally different today—both only expose a `FeatureBuildItem`. There are two because Quarkus extensions are packaged as runtime + deployment pairs, and `pathland-quarkus-kotlin` was set up as its own extension rather than a plain starter.

Is the second one necessary? For the **current architecture**, yes—removing the deployment module would break `pathland-quarkus-kotlin` as a Quarkus extension. Semantically, it is optional: since there are no Kotlin-specific build steps, `pathland-quarkus-kotlin` could be reduced to a **plain starter POM** (`pathland-quarkus` + `pathland-view-kotlin` + `quarkus-kotlin`), and then `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment` and `PathlandKotlinProcessor` could be deleted. The trade-off is losing the distinct `pathland-kotlin` feature listing and a place for future Kotlin build-time integration.
So none of it are remnants of JAva dsl?

No. The only Java-DSL remnants were `pathland-quarkus-java`, `pathland-quarkus-java-deployment` (`PathlandJavaProcessor`), and `pathland-quarkus-starter` — all already deleted.

- `PathlandProcessor` was created in commit `7aacc67a` for the **DSL-neutral core extension** (`pathland-quarkus`), not the Java DSL.
- `PathlandKotlinProcessor` was added in `f697e079` with the **Kotlin DSL extension**; it is the build-time half of `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`.

`PathlandProcessor`’s javadoc still says “until a DSL-specific build step needs to be added”, which reflects the pre-split history, but the class itself is core Quarkus extension plumbing, not Java DSL code.
Why do we have both pathland-quarkus-demo and pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo?

# --- Same-server proxy demo (spec/PROXY.md) ------------------------------------
# The music player at / embeds the small ad app mounted at /ad (this same server)
# as a sponsored slot in its Now Playing pane, via a ProxyView. This is the origin
# app's base URL the player proxies; point it at another host/port to proxy a
# remote app instead.
pathland.demo.ad-url=http://localhost:8080/ad

# --- Per-window id on the first request (issue #155) ---------------------------
# Opt the DOM client into the service worker that attaches the per-window id to
# top-level navigations, so the SSR renders the right persisted-state scope on the
# FIRST paint (instead of defaults that the live connection then corrects). The id
# never appears in the URL. Off by default; the worker is served at /_pathland/sw.js
# with Service-Worker-Allowed: / (root scope) and no-cache.
pathland.service-worker=true

# Static resources (the demo's media/icons are served from a disk extraction via
# DemoAssetsRoute, which also sends its own caching headers; this covers the rest
# of Quarkus's static resources, e.g. the DOM client bundle).
quarkus.http.static-resources.max-age=168h

# Pathland SSR debug comments: when true, every rendered HTML node is prefixed
# with a comment naming its component type and the modifiers applied, e.g.
#   <!-- #1 VStack: spacing=4, alignment=Fill -->
# Debugging aid — opt-in; the live /ws deltas are unaffected.

# --- Observability (issue #62) -------------------------------------------------
# Structured (JSON) console logging — the production-shaped reference app default.

# Metrics: Micrometer counters/timers at pathland.* are exposed at /q/metrics

#

They were added at different times for different purposes, and now overlap heavily.

**History**
- `pathland-quarkus-demo` is the original Quarkus integration demo. It uses the DSL-neutral `pathland-quarkus` extension, is a **Java host**, and is the production-shaped demo: two mounted apps (`/` + `/ad`), same-server proxy, extracted assets route, JSON logging, metrics, and `ProxyDemoTest`.
- `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo` was added with the Kotlin DSL extension (`f697e079` → demo `c67b7f0f`) to prove the Kotlin-only path: Kotlin host, Kotlin CDI/all-open build, `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`, and a DOM-bundle/SSR smoke test.

**Current reality**
- Both mount the same `MusicPlayerView`. The Kotlin demo’s own `KotlinDemoView` is dead code — `newRoot()` returns `MusicPlayerView()` and `KotlinDemoView` is commented out.
- The Kotlin demo’s remaining unique value is build/extension coverage (`pathland-quarkus-kotlin`, Kotlin all-open, Kotlin CDI) plus `KotlinDemoSmokeTest`.
- The Java demo’s unique value is Java-host mounting, multi-app/proxy behavior, assets, and observability.

**Recommendation**
- Keep `pathland-quarkus-demo` as the single reference Quarkus app — it proves the Java-host requirement and exercises the harder features.
- Either:
  1. keep `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo`, but make it mount `KotlinDemoView` so it actually demonstrates Kotlin-only authoring, or
  2. delete it and rely on the `pathland-quarkus-kotlin` extension tests, or
  3. collapse `pathland-quarkus-kotlin` into a plain starter (then delete its demo + deployment module).

If maintenance cost matters most, option 3 gives one Quarkus demo, one deployment module, and no duplicate full app.

content.text:
Not cleanly as a simple rename. `KotlinView` and `View` are two different things:

- `dev.pathland.view.core.View` (`pathland-view-core`) is the SPI type that **all builders return** (`Text`, `VStack`, …).
- `KotlinView` (`pathland-view-kotlin/.../KotlinView.kt:25`) is the **abstract composite base** that adds `body()`, state delegates, and auto-registration.

If you rename `KotlinView` → `View`, you get two `View` types. That immediately breaks the normal app shape:

```kotlin
class MyHomeView : View() {
    override fun body(): View = VStack { ... } // VStack returns core View, not dsl View
}
```

`VStack` returns `dev.pathland.view.core.View`, which is **not** a subtype of the new abstract `dsl.View`. To make it compile you’d have to either:

1. use inferred return types (`override fun body() = VStack { ... }`) and alias core imports as `CoreView` everywhere, or
2. change all DSL builders to return the new `dsl.View` type, or
3. rename the core SPI (`core.View` → `ViewNode`/`ViewContent`) and make the DSL base the only `View`.

Option 3 is the coherent endpoint, but it is a cross-module, breaking redesign of the engine/SPI — much larger than a rename.

**Recommendation:** drop the historical `Kotlin` prefix with a name that doesn’t collide:

- `Component` — short and idiomatic
- `CompositeView` — precise: a view with a `body()`
- `ViewComponent` — explicit but verbose

My preference is `CompositeView` if you want accuracy, or `Component` if you want brevity. The change is then limited to ~10 main files, 4 tests, demo views, and docs.

If you specifically want the public API to read `class Foo : View()`, I’d plan the larger option 3 separately: rename `core.View` to a node/SPI name, make the DSL base `View`, and update all builders/consumers. That is a big API break, but it is the only version that avoids two competing `View` names.

gh issue create --title "investigate: align the Kotlin DSL with SwiftUI's View protocol" --label enhancement --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Following #169, `KotlinView` was renamed to `Component` because `dev.pathland.view.core.View` is already the JVM SPI type. Investigate whether the Kotlin DSL should instead align with SwiftUI's model, where **`View` is the single public protocol/type** and composite views simply conform to it.

This is an investigation/decision issue, not an implementation task.

## Current state

- `dev.pathland.view.core.View` — the core protocol-like interface; all DSL builders (`Text`, `VStack`, …) return this type.
- `dev.pathland.view.dsl.Component` — an abstract composite base adding `body()`, state delegates, and builder auto-registration.
- The two concepts currently coexist under different names.

## Options to evaluate

1. **Keep `Component`** — no redesign; accept a stateful composite base alongside the core `View` interface.
2. **SwiftUI-style `View`** — make `View` the sole public authoring type. Rename the core SPI (`View` → `ViewNode`/`Element`), have primitives and composites conform to the public `View`, and move state/body support into delegates/composition/opaque return types.
3. **Compose-style** — drop the base class and author with composable-style functions plus `remember`-style state; largest redesign.
4. **Hybrid** — keep `Component` but expose a `View` interface/name for public signatures; assess whether this is actually better or just adds ambiguity.

## Questions

- Can a Kotlin `View` protocol carry `body()` and persisted state without a base class, or do delegates/interfaces suffice?
- What is the SwiftUI `some View` analog in Kotlin, and does it materially improve composition?

## Plan: mount `AdView` in the Kotlin Quarkus demo

Assuming you want parity with `pathland-quarkus-demo`: mount `AdView` at `/ad` **and** have `MusicPlayerView` embed it via `ProxyView`.

### 1. Update `KotlinDemoApplication.kt`

- Add `@ConfigProperty(name = "pathland.demo.ad-url", defaultValue = "http://localhost:8080/ad")`.
- Change the root from `MusicPlayerView()` to `MusicPlayerView.make(adUrl)`.
- Add a `MountedApp` producer:

```kotlin
@Produces
@Singleton
fun adApp(): MountedApp =
    MountedApp.of("/ad", PathlandApp { AdView() })
```

`PathlandRegistryProducer` already injects `Instance<MountedApp>` and mounts each at its subpath, so no extension changes are needed.

### 2. Config

Add to `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo/src/main/resources/application.properties`:

```properties
pathland.demo.ad-url=http://localhost:8080/ad
```

Add `src/test/resources/application.properties`:

```properties
quarkus.http.test-port=8081
pathland.demo.ad-url=http://localhost:8081/ad
```

The test port must be pinned because the proxy origin is an absolute loopback URL, same as the Java demo.

### 3. Tests

Extend `KotlinDemoSmokeTest` (or add `AdProxyDemoTest.kt`) with the Java demo’s proxy assertions:

- SSR at `/` contains `Pathland Ads`.
- SSR contains `Clicked 0 times`.
- The ad subtree is remapped into the proxy id range, e.g. `data-pathland-id="1073741825"`.
- Optionally assert `/ad` itself returns 200 and renders the ad directly.

### 4. Docs/status

- Update `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo/status.md`:
  - `AdView` mounted at `/ad`.
  - Embedded into the player via `ProxyView`.
  - Update the verified-by test list.
- Update the Kotlin demo description in `AGENTS.md`/`README.md` if it says only `MusicPlayerView`.

### 5. Verification

- `mvn -q -B -pl pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo -am test`
- `mvn -q -B test`
- Run `scripts/run-quarkus-kotlin-demo.sh` and verify:
  - `/` shows the player with the sponsored ad in the Now Playing pane.
  - `/ad` renders the standalone ad app.

### Notes / risk

- `AdView` needs no asset route; `pathland-demo-common` assets are already served from the classpath.
- The ad only appears in wide layouts where `NowPlayingSidebar` renders, matching the Java demo.
- If you only want the `/ad` mount without proxy embedding, we can skip the `adUrl` change and the proxy assertions.
